snippet.title: What Happens If You Skip Brushing at Night
snippet.description:
What happens if you skip brushing at night? Mouth germs turn leftover food into acid, and while you sleep your spit, which clears sugar and acid by day, almost stops flowing. This cartoon shows the night from the top of a tooth: the spit guards fall asleep and the germs throw a party. The fix is the NHS advice: brush last thing before bed for two minutes with fluoride toothpaste, then spit and do not rinse.

Sources:
• NHS. How to keep your teeth clean (page last reviewed 30 June 2025): https://www.nhs.uk/live-well/healthy-teeth-and-gums/how-to-keep-your-teeth-clean/
• Dawes C. Salivary flow patterns and the health of hard and soft oral tissues. J Am Dent Assoc. 2008 (PMID 18460676): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/18460676/
• NIH National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research. The Tooth Decay Process: How to Reverse It and Avoid a Cavity (reviewed January 2025): https://www.nidcr.nih.gov/health-info/tooth-decay/more-info/tooth-decay-process
• NIH National Institute of Dental and Craniofacial Research. Tooth Decay (reviewed September 2025): https://www.nidcr.nih.gov/health-info/tooth-decay
